instrument_name: Oklahoma Minimum Wage Act - 40 O.S. 197.2, 197.4, 197.5, 197.16
figure_or_rule_carried: 197.2: no employer shall pay less than the current federal minimum wage for all hours worked (no state-specific rate; floor = FLSA rate). 197.4(d): Act covers employers with more than 10 FT employees at one location OR gross business > USD 100,000/yr; does not apply to FLSA-covered employers paying the federal minimum. 197.4(e) excludes farm, domestic service in private home, federal employees, volunteers, newspaper carriers, ICC carriers, EAP and outside sales, part-time < 25 h/week not on permanent status, under-18 non-graduates and students under 22, feedstore, reserve deputies. 197.5: state employees specifically covered. 197.16 (Laws 2025 c. 401, eff. 2025-11-01): tip/meal/lodging credit allowed if cash wage >= 29 CFR 531.50(a)(1) (federal tipped cash wage).
verification_method: inspected directly (official complete-title RTF, Last-Modified 2025-12-31, converted to text and read)

instrument_name: 40 O.S. 160 - state preemption of minimum wage and mandatory vacation/sick leave
figure_or_rule_carried: Legislature occupies the field of mandated minimum wage and mandatory minimum vacation or sick leave days; no municipality or political subdivision may set a minimum wage or mandatory paid/unpaid vacation or sick leave; existing or future local ordinances null and void (municipal own-employee benefits excepted). => no local minimum wage and no local paid sick leave in Oklahoma.

instrument_name: Oklahoma Protection of Labor Act - 40 O.S. 165.1, 165.2 (current text, Laws 2022 c. 156)
figure_or_rule_carried: Second document family confirming US-OK-003 (OSCN wayback): pay non-exempt employees at least twice each calendar month on regular paydays designated in advance; state/county/municipal, school district, exempt employees and qualifying foundations at least monthly; at most 11 days between end of pay period and payday, plus 3 days grace; payment in lawful money incl. electronic means; employer may at its discretion pay by deposit at a financial institution of the employee's choice or, if the employee does not consent or designate one, to a payroll card account; with each payment a brief itemized statement of any and all deductions; dishonoured paycheck fees reimbursed within 14 days. 165.1(7) wages include holiday and vacation pay, severance, bonuses agreed upon or provided in an established policy.
verification_method: second independent authority (Legislature complete-title file vs OSCN copy in US-OK-003)

instrument_name: 40 O.S. 165.3 - Termination of employee - payment - failure to pay
figure_or_rule_carried: Whenever employment terminates (discharge or resignation alike), wages in full, less offsets and amounts in bona fide disagreement, are due at the next regular designated payday for the period worked, via regular pay channels or by certified mail if the employee requests; CBA may provide otherwise. Willful failure: liquidated damages 2% of unpaid wages per day, capped at the unpaid wages.

instrument_name: Employment Security Act of 1980 - 40 O.S. 1-201(48) taxable wages; 1-223 applicable percentages; 3-102 contributions
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wage base = applicable percentage of the state average annual wage for the second preceding calendar year, rounded to nearest USD 100; applicable percentage by conditional factor: none 40%, A 41.25%, B 42.5%, C 43.75%, D 45%. Taxable wages count wages for services covered by this act or other state unemployment compensation acts (=> wages already reported to another state in the year count toward the OK base). Contributions are employer-only and shall not be deducted from wages (3-102(A)); fractions of a cent: < 0.5 cent dropped, >= 0.5 cent up (3-102(B)); rate notice by 30 Sept of prior year, appeal 20 days.

instrument_name: 40 O.S. 1-218 Wages (UI) and 1-210 employment coverage thresholds
figure_or_rule_carried: UI wages = all remuneration incl. cash value of non-cash remuneration and tips; anything the IRC treats as wages is UI wages. Excluded: employer payments for retirement (but employee 401(k)/403(b)/408(k)/457/408(p) deferrals ARE wages), sickness/accident disability, medical, qualifying death benefits, thrift funds; s.125 cafeteria payments; s.127/s.129 assistance; employer-paid FICA on domestic/agricultural; non-required dismissal pay; meals and lodging for employer convenience on premises; SUB plan payments. Coverage: agricultural labor if USD 20,000 cash in a quarter or 10+ workers in 20 weeks; domestic service if USD 1,000 cash in a quarter.

instrument_name: 40 O.S. 2-802 Reports by employers - New hire registry
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers doing business in Oklahoma report to OESC every hire who resides or works in Oklahoma: employee name, address, SSN, date of employment, state of employment; employer name, address, FEIN. Within 20 days of hire, or if electronic, twice monthly 12-16 days apart; by copy of W-4, fax, electronic media or other approved means. DHS Child Support Services is the official New Hire Registry and gets data from OESC. Employee/employer per IRC 3401.

instrument_name: 40 O.S. 173.1 Employers' use of social security numbers
figure_or_rule_carried: Private employing entities in Oklahoma may not publicly post/display an employee SSN, print it on access cards, require transmission over the Internet unless secure/encrypted, require it for website login without a password/PIN, or print it on materials mailed to the employee unless state or federal law requires it on the document. State and political subdivisions exempt. Internal verification/administrative use and uses required by law allowed; employee may consent in writing. No explicit pay-statement SSN-truncation rule.

instrument_name: 68 O.S. 2355 Tax imposed - individual rates tax year 2026 (Laws 2025 c. 307)
figure_or_rule_carried: TY2026+: single/MFS 0% on first 3,750; 2.5% next 1,150; 3.5% next 2,300; 4.5% remainder. MFJ/QSS/HoH: 0% first 7,500; 2.5% next 2,300; 3.5% next 4,600; 4.5% remainder. (E) each rate cut by 0.25 pp per State Board of Equalization certification under 62 O.S. 34.103(D) (revenue trigger), deferred if revenue failure declared (F). (G) nonresident aliens: 8% tax and 8% withholding on amounts covered by that subsection, quarterly return by last day of month after quarter. Resident AND nonresident individuals taxed on Oklahoma taxable income.
verification_method: derived arithmetically (OW-2 2026 annual table thresholds 10,100/11,250/13,550 single and 20,200/22,500/27,100 married = standard deduction 6,350/12,700 (68 O.S. 2358) + statutory band edges; tier amounts 28.75/109.25 and 57.50/218.50 reproduced)

instrument_name: 68 O.S. 2385.1, 2385.2, 2385.3 Withholding - definitions, amount, remittance, statements, annual reconciliation
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee = resident individual performing services within or without Oklahoma + any other individual performing services within Oklahoma; corporate officers and government officials included. Wages = IRC wages except: farm work <= USD 900/month; domestic service in private home/college club/fraternity; non-trade/business work < USD 200 cash/quarter; nonresident with <= USD 300 Oklahoma income in a quarter; ministers/religious orders. 2385.2: table devised by OTC; no withholding if < USD 0.25 per quarter; gambling winnings 4%. 2385.3: quarterly return by 20th of month after quarter; federal semiweekly depositors remit on federal semiweekly dates and file via EDI; avg >= USD 500/quarter prior FY -> monthly by 20th; < 500 -> quarterly by 20th. W-2 to employee by 31 Jan, or within 30 days of last wage payment if terminated mid-year. Annual reconciliation to OTC by 31 Jan via EDI; penalty up to USD 1,000 if > 30 days late. Withheld sums held in trust.

instrument_name: 68 O.S. 2358 (v1-v3) Oklahoma standard deduction from tax year 2017
article_or_section: 68 O.S. 2358(A)(2)(g) - identical in all three published versions v1/v2/v3
figure_or_rule_carried: Standard deduction (not indexed): 6,350 single/MFS; 12,700 MFJ/QSS; 9,350 head of household. Personal exemption 1,000 (OW-2 allowance = 1,000 / pay periods).

instrument_name: 12 O.S. 1171.2 child support limits/priority; 1173.4 continuing earnings garnishment
figure_or_rule_carried: Child support max: 50% of disposable earnings if supporting another spouse/child, 60% if not; +5 pp (55%/65%) for arrears older than 12 weeks. Priority with NMSN: current child and spousal support, health premiums, arrearages, other. Continuing earnings garnishment: lien on earnings for 180 days; garnishee answers and pays within 7 days after each pay period; prior lien has priority; if already under child-support assignment, creditor garnishment = state max % minus % withheld for support, not over 25%; amounts withheld for higher-priority statutory debts reduce the garnishment.

instrument_name: 31 O.S. 1(A)(18) exemption of 75% of current earnings
figure_or_rule_carried: 75% of all current wages or earnings for personal services earned in the last 90 days is exempt from attachment, except in child-support garnishment under Title 12 (so creditor garnishment max 25%, subject to the federal CCPA 30x minimum-wage floor, whichever protects more).

instrument_name: OAC 710:90 (2026 edition) - OK-W-4 rule, default status, NRA 8%, employee statement content, records, return/remittance schedule
figure_or_rule_carried: 1-5: federal W-4 executed before 2018-03-01 still governs OK status/allowances; employees starting after 2018-02-28 or changing withholding submit Oklahoma Form W-4 (OK-W-4). 1-7(f): no OK-W-4 -> withhold as single with zero allowances; 1-7(c) extra withholding by written agreement; 1-7(e) employer must inform employees of options. 1-8: nonresident aliens 8% of Oklahoma taxable income paid. 1-10: annual statement shows employer name, employee name, LAST FOUR digits of SSN (XXX-XX-1234 or ***-**-1234), wages subject to tax, tax withheld; by 31 Jan, or within 30 days of last wage payment on termination. 1-11: records kept at least 4 years after due date/payment. 3-4: quarterly return by 20th of month after quarter on calendar-year basis, zero returns required; monthly remittance after any quarter with > USD 500 withheld; semiweekly federal depositors follow federal dates (3 banking days) and file via EDI. 1-6 supplemental: highest rate of 68 O.S. 2355 (cross-reference to 2355(B)(1) is stale; TY2026 top rate is 4.5% under 2355(D), US-OKS5-009) or aggregate method.

instrument_name: 12 O.S. 1171.3 Income assignment proceedings (child support IWO)
figure_or_rule_carried: Income assignment effective on next payment after notice; remit to the Centralized Support Registry within 7 days after the obligor is paid, with the withholding date; notify the payee agency within 10 days of the obligor's termination (last-known address, new employer if known); employer fee up to USD 5 per pay period, max USD 10 per month, deductible from the obligor's earnings.

instrument_name: 40 O.S. 196.1-196.14 Oklahoma Minimum Wages on Public Works Act - unconstitutional and repealed
figure_or_rule_carried: Entire state prevailing wage act held unconstitutional in City of Oklahoma City v. State ex rel. Oklahoma Dept. of Labor, 918 P.2d 26 (Okla. 1995); sections repealed by Laws 2015 c. 71, eff. 2015-11-01. No state prevailing wage / certified payroll obligation; only federal Davis-Bacon on federally funded work. Confirms US-OK-P5-1-001 from the primary source.

instrument_name: 40 O.S. 71-89 Child labor (hours, rest periods, certificates)
figure_or_rule_carried: Under 16: only FLSA-permitted occupations; outside agriculture/domestic service max 3 h on a school day, 8 h non-school day, 18 h/week in session (first Tuesday after Labor Day to 31 May), 40 h/week otherwise; 1 h cumulative rest per 8 consecutive hours and no more than 5 consecutive hours without 30 min rest. No state overtime rule: the Minimum Wage Act (197.1-197.17) has no overtime section; overtime follows FLSA.
verification_method: inspected directly (section list 197.1-197.17 read: no overtime provision)

instrument_name: OESC Important Numbers for 2027 + Contribution Rates page (2027 table)
figure_or_rule_carried: 2027: no conditional factor; state experience factor 29%; range of rates 0.1% to 5.5%; taxable wage base USD 24,400; new employer rate 1.5% (until 4 quarters of experience within a rate cycle; 4 consecutive no-wage reports revert to new-employer rate); max weekly benefit 703; max benefit amount 11,248; max benefit wage charge 33,744; average annual wage 60,993.99; average weekly wage 1,172.96. Rate notice OES-048 end of September; protest OES-048P within 20 days; rates 3.4%+ cannot rise more than 2 pp in two years. G-DERIVE: 40% x 60,993.99 = 24,397.60 -> nearest 100 = 24,400 (40 O.S. 1-201(48), 1-223(1), US-OKS5-005).

instrument_name: OESC Important Numbers for 2025 (derivation anchor for wage-base percentages)
figure_or_rule_carried: 2025: conditional factor D, state factor 50%; rates 0.3% to 9.2%; taxable wage base 28,200; new employer 1.50%; average annual wage 56,341.77. Derivation: 50% x 56,341.77 = 28,170.89 -> 28,200; 2026 (US-OK-002): 42.5% x 58,765.95 = 24,975.53 -> 25,000. Both reproduce only with the percentages 42.5% (A) and 50% (D), i.e. the 1-223 schedule BEFORE Laws 2025 c. 140 (eff. 2025-11-01), which now reads A 41.25% / D 45%. The pre-amendment text itself was not read (inference from arithmetic).

instrument_name: OESC OES-047 Quarterly Wage Report Instructions (pub. 10-2024) - ICESA upload specification
article_or_section: ICESA record types; Technical requirements; E/S/T/P layouts
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly wage report (OES-3 Employer's Quarterly Contribution Report) filed online via EZ Tax Express (manual entry or upload). Upload format = NASWA/ICESA, 275-character fixed-length records, non-delimited ASCII .txt, CR/LF terminated; required records E (employer), S (employee wage: name as on SS card, upper case, SSN, total and taxable wages), T (totals incl. state quarter UI taxes due); P (payment) optional for TPAs; zero-wage report = E + T. Required on every active account even with no wages. Late: USD 200 + 10% of contributions if not filed within 15 days of Notice of Non-Receipt OES-054; interest 1%/month (wage-reporting page, Last Modified 2025-12-16).

instrument_name: Form OK-W-4 Employee's State Withholding Allowance Certificate (Revised 3-2021)
figure_or_rule_carried: Fields: name, SSN, address, filing status (Single / Married / Married but withhold at higher Single rate); line 1 self allowance, 2 spouse allowance (0 if spouse works), 3 dependents, 4 additional allowances, 5 total allowances, 6 additional withholding per pay period (USD), 7 Exempt (no liability last year and this year), 8 Exempt under SCRA/MSRRA with Form OW-9-MSE, 9 Exempt for active-duty military income deduction. Not mailed to OTC. Form text: amounts not taxed 1,000 exemption + 6,350 standard deduction single; 2,000 + 12,700 MFJ.

instrument_name: Oklahoma Department of Labor - FAQs Wage and Hour (Last Modified 2026-02-18)
article_or_section: FAQ items: minimum wage, coverage, pay frequency, overtime, pay stub, direct deposit, final pay, deductions, benefits, breaks, jury duty, prevailing wage
figure_or_rule_carried: State and federal minimum wage USD 7.25/h (since 2000-07-24 per page; FLSA rate 2009); state law applies to employers with 10+ FT employees or gross > USD 100,000 unless federally covered. Overtime only via FLSA (1.5x over 40/week). Pay stub required with each payment, paper or electronic. Employer may require direct deposit but cannot mandate a particular bank unless cash/check also offered; payroll debit cards must be voluntary. Final pay: next regular payday whether quit or fired. Deductions beyond statute/court order need a written agreement signed by both (loan/advance/overpayment, merchandise, uniforms, insurance, retirement, breakage/shortage where employee solely responsible). No mandatory benefits law (vacation per established policy). No breaks for 16+; jury duty unpaid for non-exempt. State prevailing wage unconstitutional.

instrument_name: 26 O.S. 7-101 Employees to be allowed time to vote
figure_or_rule_carried: Registered-voter employees get 2 hours (more if distance requires) to vote on election day or an in-person absentee day; employee must notify at least 3 days before; employer may choose the hours; not applicable if the work day starts 3+ hours after polls open or ends 3+ hours before close. On proof of voting, no loss of compensation (paid time). Civil penalty USD 50-100.

instrument_name: 38 O.S. 34, 35 Jury service - employment protection and leave
figure_or_rule_carried: No termination or adverse action for jury service; employer may not require or request use of annual/vacation/sick leave; employer need not pay wages for jury absence unless the employee chooses to use paid leave (employee's decision). Misdemeanor fine up to USD 5,000 and civil damages. (FLSA salary-basis rule for exempt staff per ODOL FAQ US-OKS5-022.)

instrument_name: 62 O.S. 34.103(D) income tax rate-reduction trigger (Laws 2025 c. 307, HB 2764)
article_or_section: 62 O.S. 34.103(D)(1)-(3) and uncodified s.3 of Laws 2025 c. 307
figure_or_rule_carried: First possible 0.25 pp cut of every 68 O.S. 2355(D) rate: State Board of Equalization preliminary certification in December 2026, final certification in February 2027, reduction effective the 1 January after the final February certification (=> earliest 2028-01-01). December 2026 meeting must also certify FY2027 first-5.5-month revenues within 95% of the February 2026 estimate and no revenue failure. => TY2027 rates are the TY2026 rates (0/2.5/3.5/4.5) unless new law. Operating level: rate change flows into OTC withholding tables (withholding) and assessment.

figure_or_rule_carried: SB 277 (paid leave proposal): committee substitute, title stricken, referred to Appropriations 2026-02-24, no later action - NOT ENACTED (2025-26 Legislature). instrument_name: 40 O.S. 1-210 Employment - UI exclusions for special populations
figure_or_rule_carried: UI not 'employment': churches/church-controlled organisations and religious schools; ministers and members of religious orders; elected officials (and other listed governmental roles); inmates; agricultural labor below the 1-210(5) thresholds (H-2A nonresident aliens excluded); domestic service below USD 1,000/quarter; service for one's son, daughter or spouse and a child under 21 for a parent; federal service; student nurses and interns; insurance agents and licensed real-estate agents on commission; newspaper carriers under 18; students (and spouses in aid programmes) employed by their own school; students in work-study programmes; cotton choppers. Localisation per 1-210(1)-(4) (multistate) follows the uniform test.

instrument_name: Oklahoma Tax Commission Newsroom (bulletin sweep 2026-01-01 to 2026-11-02)
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 items listed: filing season (2026-03-02), Parental Choice Tax Credit (2026-01-15), monthly collections releases through October 2026. No withholding-table change, new withholding form or employer-filing change announced in 2026. OW-2 (Rev. 11-2025) remains the current table for 2026.

instrument_name: OESC New Hire Reporting page (Oklahoma Employer New Hire Reporting System)
figure_or_rule_carried: Report every new hire to OESC within 20 days of start date (start = first day services performed for wages) via the online Oklahoma Employer New Hire Reporting System (Tyler Technologies). Required: employee name, address, SSN, date started, state of hire; optional: OESC account number, occupation and salary, date of birth, dependent health insurance availability, still employed?, recall/rehire date. Report the payroll processing address (IWOs are sent there). Rehires/recalls reported as recalled; hires who quit before the due date still reported. Multistate employers may elect single-state reporting via OCSE.
verification_method: second independent authority (agency page vs statute 40 O.S. 2-802, US-OKS5-007)
